cd $WS/confit; make build >/tmp/build.log 2>&1; echo build=$?; make unit >/tmp/unit.log 2>&1; echo unit=$?

answer:
**Not everything passes.** `make build && make unit && make component` stops at `make unit`, so `make component` never runs in the chain. I ran the three steps separately to see each result.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `make build` | Passes. It prints NU1902 warnings about a moderate-severity vulnerability in `Scriban.Signed` 7.2.0. |
| `make unit` | Fails with 1 failing test, which fails on both net10.0 and net9.0. 271 of 272 tests pass per framework. |
| `make component` | Passes, 20 of 20. This was run on its own and wouldn't have run in your chained command. |

**Failing test:** `ConfIT.UnitTest.Util.DeltaFormatterTests.Format_FieldInActualNotInExpected_ShowsAbsentSentinel`, at `test/ConfIT.UnitTest/Util/DeltaFormatterTests.cs:53`.

The failure is the same on both frameworks. The assertion expected the formatted diff to contain `<absent>`:

```
Expected result "Response body mismatch:

debug
  expected: <not present>
  actual:   "trace"" to contain "<absent>".
```

`DeltaFormatter` now prints `<not present>` for a field that is in the actual response but not in the expected one. The test still looks for the old `<absent>` sentinel. I didn't check which side is out of date, the formatter or the test. I didn't modify any files.
